headline: 9-wicket win: Bangladesh secures historic Test victory over Australia in Darwin
summary: Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto describes the dominant four-day performance as the biggest win in the nation's cricket history.
details: Bangladesh achieved a landmark nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, dominating the hosts across all facets of the game to win in just four days.
The Tigers bowled Australia out for 198 in the first innings before posting a massive 426, securing a commanding 228-run lead.
Australia was dismissed for 284 in their second innings, leaving Bangladesh to chase a small target of 57, which they reached in 14.2 overs.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto named the entire team as his 'Player of the Match,' praising the collective effort of both the batting and bowling units.
Shanto highlighted the crucial contributions of the lower-order batters—Hasan, Taijul, Taskin, and Ebadot—who helped push the first-innings total beyond 400.
The victory was hailed as a historic upset, with Australian captain Pat Cummins admitting his side was 'outplayed in all facets' of the match.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, recognizing the magnitude of the win on Australian soil.
This victory marks a significant milestone for Bangladesh, ending a 21-year wait for a Test win against Australia outside of Cardiff.
caption:
A historic upset in Darwin! 🇧🇩
Bangladesh just secured what Captain Shanto calls the biggest victory in the nation's cricket history.

Bangladesh achieved a landmark nine-wicket victory over Australia in Darwin, dominating the hosts across all facets of the game to win in just four days.

The Tigers bowled Australia out for 198 in the first innings before posting a massive 426, securing a commanding 228-run lead.

Australia was dismissed for 284 in their second innings, leaving Bangladesh to chase a small target of 57, which they reached in 14.2 overs.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto named the entire team as his 'Player of the Match,' praising the collective effort of both the batting and bowling units.

Shanto highlighted the crucial contributions of the lower-order batters—Hasan, Taijul, Taskin, and Ebadot—who helped push the first-innings total beyond 400.

The victory was hailed as a historic upset, with Australian captain Pat Cummins admitting his side was 'outplayed in all facets' of the match.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina congratulated the team via video call, recognizing the magnitude of the win on Australian soil.

This victory marks a significant milestone for Bangladesh, ending a 21-year wait for a Test win against Australia outside of Cardiff.

headline: At least 2 years to resolve fuel crisis, says Finance Minister
summary: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury warns that immediate solutions to gas and electricity shortages are not possible given the current economic state.
details: Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury stated that there is no immediate or quick fix for the ongoing gas and electricity crisis in Bangladesh.
Speaking at an American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) event on Sunday, he noted that the country's overall economic situation is not in a good state.
The Minister explained that even if new effective initiatives are taken now, it may take at least two years for the country to see the full benefits of such measures.
He highlighted that while the country has sufficient power generation capacity, a large portion of produced electricity is not being utilized correctly due to weaknesses in the transmission system.
To address this, the government is working on creating a sustainable and balanced energy mix involving gas, coal, and renewable energy.

Regarding the banking sector, the Minister emphasized the need for bank restructuring and alternative financing systems rather than relying solely on government assistance to resolve financial complexities and high default loans.
caption:
No quick fix for the energy crisis: the Finance Minister warns it will take at least 2 years to see results.

Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury stated that there is no immediate or quick fix for the ongoing gas and electricity crisis in Bangladesh.

Speaking at an American Chamber of Commerce in Bangladesh (AmCham) event on Sunday, he noted that the country's overall economic situation is not in a good state.

The Minister explained that even if new effective initiatives are taken now, it may take at least two years for the country to see the full benefits of such measures.

He highlighted that while the country has sufficient power generation capacity, a large portion of produced electricity is not being utilized correctly due to weaknesses in the transmission system.

To address this, the government is working on creating a sustainable and balanced energy mix involving gas, coal, and renewable energy.

Regarding the banking sector, the Minister emphasized the need for bank restructuring and alternative financing systems rather than relying solely on government assistance to resolve financial complexities and high default loans.
